chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Al-Husayn ibn Maysar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Garden of Adam (peace be upon him), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'It was a garden from the gardens of the world, in which the sun and the moon rise, and if it had been from the Gardens of the Hereafter, he would not have come out of it ever.'
ai.seo_question: Was the Garden of Adam in Paradise or on Earth?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration to distinguish between the primordial earthly garden where Adam dwelled and the eternal Paradise of the Hereafter, a key distinction in Shia exegesis. The presence of celestial bodies like the sun and moon serves as the primary indicator that this was a temporary abode within the Dunya, allowing for Adam's eventual descent to earth. This clarification resolves apparent contradictions in Quranic verses regarding the location of the 'Garden' by contextualizing it as a specific, non-eternal realm.
